objective: Deliver a polished, accessible APBRA MVP-1 business workspace and visual system over the existing private-case, conversation, reviewed-design, protected-generation and durable-history lifecycle without changing product authority, persistence or API contracts.
requirements: APBRA-170 Professional SaaS Experience & Visual System

A restrained APBRA design language with reusable visual tokens and presentation patterns for typography, spacing, surfaces, controls, states, data lists, disclosures, report cards, history and responsive layouts
A business-facing reporting workspace that clearly communicates current company, current case, current report stage, completed work and the next supported action
A polished first-use state and selected-case workspace for the existing request, evidence, understanding, confirmation, expert-reviewed-design, build, current-report and immutable-history journey
Clear distinction between the current report and subordinate historical report versions, without exposing engineering terminology in the normal business flow
Keyboard-accessible, semantic, responsive presentation evidence for desktop through narrow browser widths
adrs: APBRA-170 is a presentation-only frontend package. Existing server-derived company membership, private-case access, CSRF, idempotency, confirmation, reviewed_design_id, ReportDesign review authority, canonical TypeScript bridge/compiler, artifact access, history and current-access rechecks remain authoritative and unchanged.

The business workspace may reorganise or relabel existing supported information but cannot invent destinations, lifecycle states, AI design, ReportDesign content, authorization decisions, data or generation outcomes.
Normal business presentation hides implementation terminology; the existing Details for experts disclosure remains the bounded route for authorised MVP-1 technical intake and diagnostics.

The visual system uses maintainable CSS custom properties and reusable existing presentation patterns. It is restrained, enterprise-oriented and accessible rather than product imitation, decorative glassmorphism or a second application framework.

APBRA-170 remains local and CI only, synthetic-data only and AUD 0 cloud spend. It does not authorise Package D, a backend capability, API-contract or database change, live AI/provider integration, cloud deployment, Power BI Service/Desktop/DAX/RLS capability, projects, sharing, billing or public registration.

acceptance_criteria: The authenticated workspace has a coherent APBRA visual system and professional application shell that identifies the product, current workspace, supported navigation, account context and the active case when selected.
The empty or unselected workspace gives concise first-use orientation and a prominent supported Create report action without creating a fake destination or capability.

The report journey clearly presents goal, supporting information, understanding, confirmation, expert-reviewed-design readiness, build, current report and durable history using truthful state, next-action emphasis and completed/current/blocked distinction beyond colour alone.

A selected case has a clear identity, status and report workspace hierarchy; existing request, evidence, conversation, confirmation, expert details and private access functions remain reachable without changed authority or lifecycle behaviour.

Current report presentation is visually and semantically primary, including truthful build status, version, timestamp and protected download action. Historical output is subordinate and never presented as current.

Normal business-facing copy does not expose ConfirmedRequirementContract, generation bridge, canonical compiler, schema identifiers, internal digest or LOCAL_DETERMINISTIC_NO_MODEL_CALL; the existing Details for experts boundary remains explicit and permission-respecting.

Shared visual patterns cover control hierarchy, form labels, focus visibility, status chips, empty/loading/success/warning/error states, lists/tables, disclosures and narrow-screen presentation without excessive decoration or product imitation.

Component and browser evidence covers semantic landmarks, keyboard/focus-visible controls, accessible status/error messaging, current-versus-history distinction and responsive use at a narrower viewport.

No server-side authorization, reviewed ReportDesign trust boundary, API contract, PostgreSQL schema, canonical generation/compiler pipeline, private artifact access or Package B/C lifecycle semantic is changed or weakened.

No Package D, live provider, new report-design engine, second compiler, Power BI Service publishing, Desktop/DAX/RLS runtime claim, billing, public registration, projects, sharing, cloud resource or spend is implemented or claimed.
